last_cycle_summary: Cycle 7 delivered the M1 process-group termination slice through PR #11, squash-merged as 8877242 after both required CI runs passed. Every run now spawns as the leader of its own process group and all supervision paths (cancel, timeout, natural leader exit, error paths) SIGKILL the whole group, so shell-spawned descendants cannot outlive a run. Implemented by a Codex gpt-5.6-terra worker within a three-file allowlist (its sandbox blocked socket binding, so all red-to-green, parity, and runtime verification ran in the workspace). Independent Codex sol review found no blockers; three confirmed findings were fixed pre-merge, the biggest being that natural leader exit skipped the group kill and leaked descendants even after an accepted cancel. Flagged follow-up M1 scope: backend shutdown does not yet terminate active run groups (dev Ctrl-C semantics), run stdin remains inherited pending waiting-input work, and the post-reap pgid-reuse window is inherent to pgid-based killing. M1 remains active and incomplete for PTYs, pause/resume, waiting-input detection, backend-shutdown group cleanup, redaction/metadata, durable state, and remaining cleanup.
